calls.title: Brian Wang and Jake Heier
calls.summary: Brian Wang (organizer), Jake Heier (GrowthBook account manager), Kevin Dyer (principal data engineer), and Meridy Boyd-Clark (product owner) discussed GrowthBook's feature flagging and A/B testing platform to replace their fragmented in-house system and Firebase/GA setup, with pain points around slow manual data analysis and lack of cross-channel coherence. Next steps include setting up a Slack channel for support, internal kickoff

calls.title: Brian Wang and Jake Heier
calls.summary: Luke Sonnet (GrowthBook Head of Experiments) demoed setting up an A/B test using feature flags, experiment assignment queries, and metric fact tables in their warehouse-native platform. Brian Wang (Trade Me organizer), Michael Evans (product owner), and Amy (data engineer) discussed pain points around connecting Snowflake and validating data for a simple visual layout test on map search. Next steps: connect Snowflake, create the identifier and fact tables, then set up the experiment with Luke and Jake Heier supporting via Slack, aiming to launch next week.

From transcript: Main discussion is about GrowthBook experimentation platform, specifically analyzing results of a proof-of-concept experiment. Features discussed: Bayesian vs Frequentist, results page, power calculator, AI analysis, dimensional breakdowns, Insights tab. Pain points: need for self-service metrics library, data setup in Snowflake, product managers needing to interpret results easily.

Key participants: Brian Wang (internal host, seems to be from the customer company), Jake Heier (internal, briefly at start), Logan Bates (GrowthBook representative, explains features), Michael Evans (product manager/owner asking questions), Amy Silvester-Brooks, Amy Keighley (other participants). Roles: Brian is internal lead for this PoC, Logan is GrowthBook sales/support, Michael and others are product stakeholders.

Next steps: Jake to set up a product-focused presentation later this week (Thursday for them), invitees included. Also Brian will push for investment in building a metrics library.
